facts.text: Marion is named for Francis Marion, a brigadier general and hero of the American Revolutionary War.
The town of Marion was officially chartered by the South Carolina Legislature on December 17, 1847.
Business and transportation in Marion improved significantly with the completion of the Wilmington to Manchester Railroad in 1854.
Marion County was spared damage from Sherman's troops during the Civil War because the Big Pee Dee River was at flood stage.
The Marion County Court House, built in 1854, is the third courthouse to stand on or near its current site.
Several local sites, including the Marion High School and the Marion Historic District, are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
